newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar extends losses after weak raws.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar extends losses after weak raws.

text.p: London white sugar futures headed lower on Tuesday as a mixed group of sellers moved in to bale out of the nearby months following a downturn in sentiment on the raws market, traders said. After slight weakness earlier in the session mainly brought about by commission house sales, the spot March contract slumped below support at $310.00 and hit an intraday low of $308.00. "It's a bit of a mixed bag (of sellers)...but in general it's following New York," said one trader, citing commission house players coupled with some trade sales.
New York's spot March raws contract opened at 10.97 cents/lb, under the psychological 11.00 barrier and also just under initial support at 10.98.
Local traders said the sell-off on the raws was largely a response to Commitment of Traders data released on Monday.
At 1710 GMT March stood $3.40 lower at $308.30 and May down $3.50 at $307.00. Volume reached a solid 2,116 lots.
Fundamental news was thin on the ground although Sri Lanka and Syria both tender on Wednesday to buy one cargo of white sugar for February shipment dates.
Paris futures moved in tandem with London but only the two nearby months were traded in a light overall volume of 481 lots.
March was down $3.40 at $308.00, the same as its London equivalent, and May down $4.00 at $306.60.
